data.name: Mursili
data.gender_notes: Mursili is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who dispenses justice and has a strong sense of fairness and morality. The name Mursili carries the meaning “One who dispenses justice” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Mursili usually hope their child will grow to embody one who dispenses justice and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the pursuit of truth and justice, and the desire to lead with wisdom and compassion
data.etymology: Mursili belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who dispenses justice.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mursili total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: مرسلي
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مرسلي مشتق من الفعل 'رسل' الذي يعني إرسال أو بعث. في اللغة العربية، يطلق على الشخص الذي يتم إرساله أو تعيينه لتنفيذ مهمة ما. وفي السياق الإسلامي، يمكن أن يشير إلى من يرسلهم الله تعالى لهداية الناس أو إبلاغ رسالته.

in_urdu.name: مرسلی
in_urdu.meaning: مرسلی کا مطلب ہے مرسل یا مبعوث
in_urdu.long_meaning: مرسلی نام کا مطلب ہے کسی کام کے لئے بھیجا گیا یا مقرر کیا گیا۔ یہ نام عربی زبان کے فعل 'رسل' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے بھیجنا یا ارسال کرنا۔ اسلامی سیاق و سباق میں، یہ انبیاء یا رسولوں کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جنہیں اللہ تعالیٰ انسانوں کو ہدایت دینے یا اپنا پیغام پہنچانے کے لئے بھیجاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मुर्सली
in_hindi.meaning: मुर्सली का अर्थ है दूत या प्रेषित
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुर्सली नाम का अर्थ है कोई ऐसा व्यक्ति जिसे किसी विशेष कार्य के लिए भेजा जाता है या नियुक्त किया जाता है। यह नाम अरबी भाषा के क्रिया 'रसल' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है भेजना या प्रेषित करना। इस्लामी परंपरा में, यह उन पैगंबरों या दूतों के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जिन्हें अल्लाह द्वारा मानवता को निर्देश देने या अपना संदेश पहुंचाने के लिए भेजा जाता है।

in_pashto.name: مرسلی
in_pashto.meaning: مرسلی د رالولل یا استولل معنی
in_pashto.long_meaning: د مرسلی نوم معنی دى چې د کوم کار لپاره استولل یا رالولل. دا نوم د عربي ژبې د 'رسل' فعل څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چې دى معنی يې د استولو یا رالولو. په اسلامي دود کې، دا د هغو پيغمبرانو یا رسولانو لپاره کارول کېږي چې د الله تعالی لخوا د انسانانو د هدايت او يا د هغه پيغام رسولو لپاره استولل شوي دي.

in_english.name: Mursili
in_english.meaning: Mursili means messenger or one who is sent
in_english.long_meaning: The name Mursili is derived from the Arabic root 'r-s-l', which means to send or dispatch. In Islamic tradition, it refers to prophets or messengers sent by Allah to guide humanity or convey His message. The name signifies a person who is entrusted with a mission or task, often of great importance.

historical_references.reference: Mursili II, a Hittite king who ruled from 1321 to 1295 BCE. He is known for his successful military campaigns against the Egyptians, Mitanni, and Assyrians. In 1303 BCE, he led an army to the Egyptian city of Kadesh and engaged in a decisive battle against the Egyptian pharaoh Ramses II. Although the battle ended in a stalemate, Mursili's victory at Kadesh solidified Hittite power and influence in the region.

Mursili III, a Hittite king who reigned from 1272 to 1265 BCE. He is best known for his efforts to expand Hittite territory and strengthen the empire's borders. During his reign, he successfully campaigned against the city-states of Carchemish and Qatna, expanding Hittite control over the region. He also negotiated a peace treaty with the Egyptians, ending years of conflict between the two powers.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Mursili is of significant interest in the fields of Islamic history, ancient civilizations, and culture and arts. It is best known as the name of the Hittite king Mursili II (1316–1295 BC), who ruled during the Late Hittite period. In modern contexts, Mursili is increasingly being studied across various academic platforms, particularly on Academia.edu, ResearchGate, and Google Scholar. These platforms facilitate the sharing of research papers, articles, and other scholarly work related to Mursili and the Hittite civilization. The trends reflect an increased interest in understanding the historical and cultural contexts of the ancient world and its impact on modern societies. Researchers often engage in interdisciplinary studies that combine archaeology, history, linguistics, and other fields to shed light on the complexities of the past. Through these collaborative efforts, the legacy of Mursili and the Hittite civilization continue to be explored and appreciated in the 21st century.
